nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A developer is building an ASP.NET Core web app that must run on Linux container?
flashcards.back: Azure App Service is a fully managed PaaS that natively supports Linux containers, custom domains with free TLS certificates, deployment slots for staging/production swaps and built-in authentication via Easy Auth. VMs would require manual setup, Batch is for HPC workloads and Service Fabric is for microservices clusters but lacks native deployment slots and Easy Auth.

flashcards.front: An application stores millions of small JSON documents that must be queried by p?
flashcards.back: Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed multi-model database that guarantees single-digit-millisecond reads/writes and 99.999% availability. The NoSQL API is ideal for JSON documents queried by partition key. Table Storage is cheaper but lacks global distribution and SLAs on latency. Azure SQL is relational. Redis is volatile cache, not durable primary storage.

flashcards.front: Which Cosmos DB consistency level provides the strongest consistency while still?
flashcards.back: Strong consistency in Cosmos DB is incompatible with multi-region writes — it requires a single write region. Bounded Staleness is the strongest level that supports multi-region writes: reads lag behind writes by at most K versions or T time. Session is the default per-session consistency. Eventual is the weakest.

flashcards.front: A developer wants an Azure Function to run on the first day of every month at 03?
flashcards.back: Azure Functions Timer triggers use 6-field NCRONTAB syntax: {second} {minute} {hour} {day} {month} {day-of-week}. "0 0 3 1 * *" means second=0, minute=0, hour=3, day-of-month=1, every month, any day-of-week — exactly the first day of every month at 03:00. Queue/HTTP/Event Grid triggers don't have native cron scheduling.

A developer must grant a web app running on App Service permission to read secrets from Azure Key Vault WITHOUT storing any credentials in code or config. Which approach is correct?
pairs.option: Use a service principal with a client secret stored in Git

pairs.option: HTTP trigger called by an external scheduler

pairs.stem: Which Cosmos DB consistency level provides the strongest consistency while still allowing multi-region writes?

pairs.option: Azure Blob Storage with the Static website feature

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: An application needs to receive a notification within seconds when a new blob is?
flashcards.back: Azure Event Grid natively integrates with Storage and pushes Blob Created events with subject prefixes/suffixes filters, allowing low-latency, server-push notifications. Polling is wasteful and slow. Storage Queue requires the uploader to write the message manually. Service Bus topics aren't connected to Storage events out of the box. filtered on subject ending in .jpg

flashcards.front: Which Azure messaging service guarantees FIFO ordering AND duplicate detection w?
flashcards.back: Service Bus queues support sessions (ordered, FIFO delivery per session ID) and duplicate detection (rejects messages with the same MessageId within a 1-min to 7-day window). Storage Queues offer best-effort FIFO with no session/dedup. Event Hubs preserves order per partition but has no dedup. Event Grid is push-event distribution, not ordered messaging.

flashcards.front: A web API protects endpoints with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). A daemon servic?
flashcards.back: Client Credentials flow is designed for service-to-service / daemon scenarios with no user — the client authenticates with its own credentials (client ID + secret or certificate) to obtain an access token. Authorization Code is for interactive users, Implicit is deprecated, Device Code is for input-constrained user devices.

flashcards.front: Which Microsoft Graph permission type should a multi-tenant SaaS app request to ?
flashcards.back: Delegated permissions act on behalf of the signed-in user and are scoped to that user's mailbox. Mail.Read (delegated) is the least-privileged scope needed. Application permissions are app-only (no user) and access ALL mailboxes — overkill and require admin consent. Choose delegated whenever a user is signed in.

pairs.stem: A web API protects endpoints with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). A daemon service running on a VM must call the API without any user interaction. Which OAuth 2.0 flow is appropriate?
Which Azure App Configuration feature lets a developer roll out a new feature to 10% of users and progressively increase the rollout WITHOUT redeploying the app?
A developer wants to deliver a dynamic web app globally with low latency, automatic HTTPS, custom domains and a managed CDN — without provisioning a CDN profile manually. Which option is BEST?
Which Azure messaging service guarantees FIFO ordering AND duplicate detection within a configurable time window?
pairs.option: Service Bus queue with sessions and duplicate detection enabled

pairs.stem: An application needs to receive a notification within seconds when a new blob is uploaded to a container, with built-in filtering on file extension. Which Azure service provides the BEST event delivery?
pairs.option: Event Grid subscription on the storage account.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Which API Management policy should be used to throttle a specific subscription t?
flashcards.back: rate-limit (and rate-limit-by-key) enforce short-window per-subscription throttling — calls per renewal-period seconds. quota is for longer-term volume caps (e.g., per month). cors handles browser CORS. set-backend-service redirects requests. For 1,000/minute, rate-limit with calls=1000 and renewal-period=60 is correct.

flashcards.front: A developer wants to monitor an Azure Function with distributed tracing, excepti?
flashcards.back: Application Insights is the APM service for Azure apps — it captures requests, dependencies, exceptions and traces across services with correlation IDs (distributed tracing) and offers Live Metrics and Smart Detection. Azure Monitor Logs is the underlying log store but lacks APM features by itself. Service Health and Network Watcher have different purposes.

flashcards.front: Which Application Insights query language is used in the Logs blade to search te?
flashcards.back: Application Insights and Azure Monitor Logs use Kusto Query Language (KQL). Example: requests | where timestamp > ago(1h) | summarize count() by resultCode. T-SQL is for SQL DB. GraphQL is an API query language. Lucene is used by some search engines but not Azure Monitor.

flashcards.front: Which Azure Container Apps feature is BEST suited to scale a service to zero whe?
flashcards.back: Azure Container Apps uses KEDA under the hood. The HTTP scaler scales 0→N based on concurrent request volume per replica, including scale-to-zero when idle. Dapr is for service-to-service patterns, not scaling. Manual scale doesn't auto-scale. VMSS is a different compute service.
